reuse.why: Replaces the three copied category queries and setZero's view query with one getFillableCategories helper and reuses getBudgetData for copyPreviousMonth, though the template test reparses goal_def rather than relying on the tree's null-when-empty storage convention.

duplication.why: It removes the copied queries, but the hidden rule is now written twice (SQL in getFillableCategories and the JS check in copyPreviousMonth), and the template check is called from two separate paths.

placement.why: The helpers sit in budget/actions.ts beside the month-wide actions; the template-detection predicate could arguably belong with the template code.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions and their category selection are touched.

maintainability.why: Adding or changing a skip rule still means editing both getFillableCategories and copyPreviousMonth, and the per-site income check stays repeated in every action.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth keeps its own hidden/group-hidden check and calls hasSavedTemplates directly instead of sharing the fillable-category rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden/group-hidden rule appears as a SQL WHERE clause in getFillableCategories and again as a JS condition in copyPreviousMonth, the same rule reshaped across two layers.

one_place.where: The skip rule is split: getFillableCategories (SQL hidden filter + hasSavedTemplates) for setZero/set*MonthAvg, and separate inline checks in copyPreviousMonth.
